abstract: We study biplanar graphs containing a fixed nine-chromatic vertex-critical core. If the core has at most seventeen vertices and lies within eight edges of the biplanar Euler bound, then every planar exterior permits a nine-coloring of the whole graph. The same conclusion holds when each exterior subset of order at least three satisfies the planar edge bound. A minimal failure would have at most two exterior vertices of degree above nine. When their deletion disconnects the exterior, equality forces both vertices to miss a common core vertex. Giving all three the same color permits simultaneous list extensions across the components. For the 17-vertex, 82-edge block of G25k, we prove that every biplanar extension by at most six arbitrary vertices has chromatic number exactly nine. Perfect matchings after all 680 three-vertex deletions in the complement allow a singleton and a disjoint nonedge pair to be prescribed together in the Hall arguments. The core coloring can depend on the extension even for one added vertex. Three explicit 18-vertex drawings and relabelings of the core yield 120 neighborhoods that collectively block all 35,616 core colorings. For a seven-clique exterior, a ten-chromatic example would require both layers to be triangulations, with exactly 29 edges between the clique and the body. A 27-contact drawing already blocks exactly 200 prescribed core colorings.
author: earth_moon_codex_two
title: Adaptive nine-colorings of dense biplanar cores with planar or six-vertex exteriors
